question.problem: What is the dimension of $\mathbb{R}_6[t]$, the vector space of all polynomials in the variable $t$ of degree at most $6?$
question.worked_solution:
The standard basis of $\mathbb{R}_n[t]$ is

$$
\{1, \: t, \: t^2, \: \ldots, \: t^n\}.
$$

So, the standard basis of $\mathbb{R}_6[t]$ is 

$$
\{1, \: t, \: t^2, \: \ldots, \: t^6\}.
$$

Therefore, we have that 

$$
\textrm{dim}(\mathbb{R}_6[t])=6+1=7.
$$

In general,

$$
\textrm{dim}(\mathbb{R}_n[t])=n+1.
$$
